Emily — thanks for the heads up and for the procurement timeline. I understand the pause; we see this often and have a few playbook options. High level:

- We can hold the commercial terms in the MAP for a 21-day window (formalized via the attached MAP v2),
- We propose adjusting the eval/canary start by +3 weeks to accommodate the review, with a hard decision gate for the canary on the week following procurement sign-off,
- We will standby a limited pilot ramp in a reduced capacity profile to ensure you can begin lightweight testing as soon as procurement clears.

To be explicit about risks: the longer the procurement pause, the more likely we need to re-quantize the dedicated pool and re-evaluate scheduled GPU allocations (cost movement risk). I've sketched a short risk log below and attached the MAP v2 for your review.

Short risk snapshot (initial):
• Procurement hold (probable) — impact: +10–14 business days to timeline — mitigation: 21-day MAP hold + pilot staging
• Dedicated capacity re-allocation — impact: potential price delta if we rebook GPUs beyond hold window — mitigation: early re-confirm on +14 days
• Eval regression due to environment drift — impact: quality of canary results — mitigation: pre-canary smoke tests and preserved datasets

I'll cc Ben for the procurement-side conversation and Markus to confirm dedicated capacity reservation options and any credit windows we can apply.

Attached: Arcadia_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP with hold clause).

Next step: can you introduce procurement contact and a preferred time for a 30m alignment call next week?

Ben / Vanessa / Emily — quick update on capacity: we can place a soft hold on the dedicated pool for 21 calendar days with no additional charge, provided we receive a formal hold notice (email confirmation) and the signature occurs within that window. If the hold extends beyond 21 days, we will need to either (a) rebook the tranche and offer the next available slot (which may have a price increase), or (b) negotiate a nominal reservation fee to lock capacity.

Operational asks to make the hold low-friction:
• Procurement to share the assessment checklist (SOC 2 evidence list) ahead of the call,
• Arcadia to confirm preferred canary acceptance criteria (runtime SLA / token thresholds) so we can size a pilot slice,
• Redwood to provision a minimal staging environment so Arcadia can start integration tests without consuming dedicated capacity.

I'll prepare a short capacity-risk snapshot to attach to the MAP and will include a suggested credit policy if the hold window lapses due to vendor side delay.
